name: Monocular Depth Estimation Challenge (MDEC) / SYNS-Patches
description: This paper discusses the results for the second edition of the Monocular Depth Estimation Challenge (MDEC). This edition was open to methods using any form of supervision, including fully-supervised, self-supervised, multi-task or proxy depth. The challenge was based around the SYNS-Patches dataset, which features a wide diversity of environments with high-quality dense ground-truth. This includes complex natural environments, e.g. forests or fields, which are greatly underrepresented in current benchmarks. The challenge received eight unique submissions that outperformed the provided SotA baseline on any of the pointcloud- or image-based metrics. The top supervised submission improved relative F-Score by 27.62%, while the top self-supervised improved it by 16.61%. Supervised submissions generally leveraged large collections of datasets to improve data diversity. Self-supervised submissions instead updated the network architecture and pretrained backbones. These results represent a significant progress in the field, while highlighting avenues for future research, such as reducing interpolation artifacts at depth boundaries, improving self-supervised indoor performance and overall natural image accuracy.
general_score_metric: F‑Score (primary reported improvement) along with standard depth metrics such as RMSE and AbsRel
reputation: A focused challenge offering a high-quality, diverse natural-image depth dataset that attracted a small number of strong submissions and is viewed as a useful complement to indoor-centric benchmarks.
notes: Small number of submissions (eight) limits statistical breadth; multiple metrics reported (pointcloud- and image-based) so comparisons require care; not an LLM benchmark; potential for dataset-specific tuning.
